extracted.intended_audience: general readers; civic organizers and philanthropists; readers of Franklin's autobiography
extracted.subtask_description: An excerpt from Benjamin Franklin's Autobiography (Gutenberg text) recounting his civic projects, practical reforms, and anecdotes about sects, inventions, and public fundraising in mid-18th century Pennsylvania. Contains descriptive narrative and pragmatic advice embedded in memoir.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid presenting yourself as author of public schemes
rubrics_metrics.description: State publication as of public-spirited gentlemen rather than as an act of oneself: 'In the introduction to these proposals, I stated their publication, not as an act of mine, but of some publick-spirited gentlemen, avoiding as much as I could, according to my usual rule, the presenting myself to the publick as the author of any scheme for their benefit.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use modesty or anonymity when proposing civic projects to reduce personal opposition and increase acceptance; avoid self-promotion to make proposals appear collective and non-partisan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nominate trustees to prevent sectarian predominance
rubrics_metrics.description: When contributions come from multiple sects, choose trustees so no single sect predominates: 'one of each sect was appointed, viz., one Church-of-England man, one Presbyterian, one Baptist, one Moravian, etc., those, in case of vacancy by death, were to fill it by election from among the contributors.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure governance to reflect contributor diversity (explicit seats or rotation) to preserve the institution’s original, cross-sectarian intent and avoid later appropriation by one group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare public opinion with pamphlets before soliciting subscriptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Publish explanatory material distributed gratis to prepare minds prior to fundraising: 'The first step I took was to associate ... the next was to write and publish a pamphlet, entitled Proposals Relating to the Education of Youth in Pennsylvania. This I distributed among the principal inhabitants gratis.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use clear, circulated explanatory writing to educate potential donors about the project's purpose and benefits before asking for money, increasing likelihood of subscription.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divide subscriptions into yearly quotas to enlarge participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Structure pledges as small recurring quotas: 'it was to be paid in quotas yearly for five years; by so dividing it, I judg'd the subscription might be larger.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lower the immediate cost to donors by allowing multi-year payments to broaden the donor base and raise larger aggregate sums.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make public funding conditional on private subscriptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Draft legislation so government contribution is triggered only after private subscribers raise a specified capital: detailed conditional clause provided for the hospital bill requiring contributors to raise a capital stock of ------ value before the speaker could order payment of two thousand pounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use conditional legal clauses to both reassure legislators (they won’t pay alone) and to incentivize private giving by promising to match or supplement only if a threshold is met; this also leverages public money to multiply private donations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicitation order & social-proof strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Advice on whom to solicit and when: 'apply to all those whom you know will give something; next, to those whom you are uncertain whether they will give any thing or not, and show them the list of those who have given; and, lastly, do not neglect those who you are sure will give nothing.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask certain donors first to build a visible list of contributors (social proof), then approach the uncertain to capitalize on conformity; still attempt to ask even those expected to refuse because some may surprise you.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid explicit donor lists that overburden generous contributors
rubrics_metrics.description: Refused to provide a list of known generous donors to a requester: 'I thought it would be unbecoming in me, after their kind compliance with my solicitations, to mark them out to be worried by other beggars, and therefore refus'd also to give such a list.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect donors’ privacy and avoid exposing frequent donors to repetitive solicitation by third parties; preserve goodwill by not handing out lists of supporters indiscriminately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design governance succession to reflect original contributors
rubrics_metrics.description: Trustees chosen from contributors, with vacancies filled from among contributors to maintain original representation: trustees for building were to cede it to academy trustees, and vacancy rules described to avoid sectarian takeover.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embed rules for succession and replacement that maintain the founding, cross-sectional character of an institution, limiting future capture by a single faction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Share practical inventions freely rather than pursue patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Declined a patent offer on principle: '...the governor offered to give me a patent for the sole vending of them for a term of years; but I declin'd it from a principle ... That, as we enjoy great advantages from the inventions of others, we should be glad of an opportunity to serve others by any invention of ours; and this we should do freely and generously.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor open dissemination of beneficial inventions to maximize public good, bearing in mind this may allow others to profit commercially; weigh public utility against personal gain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimate true opposition by observing attendance and absenteeism
rubrics_metrics.description: Used members’ attendance as a proxy for genuine opposition: in the fire company vote Franklin notes many Quakers absent, so absence signaled lack of sincere opposition — 'as, of the twenty-two Quakers, eight were ready to vote with us, and thirteen, by their absence, manifested that they were not inclin'd to oppose the measure...'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When gauging likelihood of organized resistance, consider not only stated positions but actual behaviors (attendance, willingness to act); absence or silence can indicate passive acceptance and reduce need for confrontation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advocate small concrete conveniences as persuasion tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Framed pavement cleaning as a local convenience benefiting shops and households to persuade neighbors to pay sixpence per month: wrote and printed a paper setting forth advantages (ease in keeping houses clean, more customers, less dust in goods).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sell reforms by emphasizing everyday, practical benefits to immediate stakeholders rather than abstract civic virtues; small, tangible improvements mobilize local support and create momentum for broader projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Street-light and lamp design principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Critique of globe lamps and proposed lamp design: 'they admitted no air below; the smoke, therefore, did not readily go out above... I therefore suggested the composing them of four flat panes, with a long funnel above to draw up the smoke, and crevices admitting air below... by this means they were kept clean, and did not grow dark in a few hours... and an accidental stroke would generally break but a single pane.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design public fixtures to be maintainable: allow airflow to remove smoke, use replaceable panes rather than fragile globes, and include features that reduce routine maintenance and improve durability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational plan for street cleaning and mud removal
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical proposals: contract watchmen to sweep dust in dry seasons before shops open; sweep dust into heaps for covered carts to remove; rake mud into low 'draining' sleds to let water drain and reduce weight before transport; favor a single central gutter to concentrate runoff for self-cleaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt an organized municipal cleaning schedule (early sweeping in summer), equip scavengers with covered carts, and design street drainage (central gutter) to minimize mud and maintenance; consider constraints like street narrowness when implementing draining-sleds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use small pilot examples to convince the public (demonstration effect)
rubrics_metrics.description: Credit given to Mr. John Clifton for placing a sample lamp at his door, which convinced people to support lighting the city: 'It was by a private person, the late Mr. John Clifton, his giving a sample of the utility of lamps... that the people were first impress'd with the idea of enlighting all the city.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deploy small, visible pilot projects or prototypes to demonstrate benefits concretely and persuade a skeptical public to adopt larger-scale reforms.
